pr_title: c8d: ImageService.LoadImage: don't ignore missing platform when requested
pr_body:
- fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/48589
- relates to https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331
- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48295


Commit f143f4ec5148e71a10d074ed275af8f63caff339 introduced platform support when loading images. However when loading a specific platform variant from a tar that contains multiple, we should not ignore cases if that platform is missing.

Before this patch, the missing platform was silently ignored, potentially
loading an empty image:

    $ docker image load -i image.tar --platform=linux/riscv64
    Loaded image: alpine:latest
    
    $ docker image ls --tree
    IMAGE           ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
    alpine:latest   beefdbd8a1da           0B             0B


With this patch, an error is produced:

When loading from a multi-platform tar, and the requested platform is not present:

    $ docker image load -i image-multiple.tar --platform=linux/ppc64le
    requested platform (linux/ppc64le) not found: NotFound: content digest sha256:c7a6800e3dc569a2d6e90627a2988f2a7339e6f111cdf6a0054ad1ff833e99b0: not found

When loading from a single-platform tar containing an image that does not
match the requested platform:

    $ docker image load -i images.tar --platform=linux/ppc64le
    requested platform (linux/ppc64le) not found: image might be filtered out

issue_context.title: c8d: image load does not produce error if given platform doesn't exist
issue_context.body:
### Description

- relates to https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331
- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48295


I noticed this while writing docs for https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331 - when specifying a `--platform` and the platform does not exist in the tar-file, no error is produced;

### Reproduce

Loading the tar without specifying a platform loads all platforms that are present in the tar;

```console
$ docker image load -i image.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

$ docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                   ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest           beefdbd8a1da       20.6MB         11.1MB
├─ linux/s390x          2b5b26e09ca2       3.46MB         3.46MB
├─ linux/ppc64le        c7a6800e3dc5       3.57MB         3.57MB
├─ linux/arm64/v8       9cee2b382fe2       13.6MB         4.09MB
├─ linux/amd64          33735bd63cf8           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v6         50f635c8b04d           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v7         f2f82d424957           0B             0B
├─ linux/386            b3e87f642f5c           0B             0B
└─ linux/riscv64        80cde017a105           0B             0B
```

But when loading the same tar, and specifying an architecture that's not included, no error is produced;

```console
$ docker image rm alpine:latest
Untagged: alpine:latest
Deleted: sha256:beefdbd8a1da6d2915566fde36db9db0b524eb737fc57cd1367effd16dc0d06d

$ docker image load -i image.tar --platform=linux/riscv64
Loaded image: alpine:latest

$ docker image ls --tree
IMAGE           ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest   beefdbd8a1da           0B             0B
```


### Expected behavior

Loading the tar should produce an error that the requested platform was not found

comments: Quick look at the code; I wonder if it's the `SkipMissing()` that's unconditionally added; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/3bc752cc891a14148ed51e269bf3fd6f61073807/daemon/containerd/image_exporter.go#L254-L259

Interestingly; behavior is different when the imported archive only has a single architecture, and importing filters out all of them;

```bash
docker image save -o images.tar --platform=linux/amd64 alpine:latest
docker image rm alpine:latest

docker image load -i images.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest        33735bd63cf8       12.1MB         3.63MB
└─ linux/amd64       33735bd63cf8       12.1MB         3.63MB


docker image load -i images.tar --platform=linux/arm64
image might be filtered out
```

https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/3bc752cc891a14148ed51e269bf3fd6f61073807/vendor/github.com/containerd/containerd/images/handlers.go#L109-L138

Looks like the difference there is between the tar being a single-arch image or a multi-arch image (with a single manifest);

```bash
docker image load -i image-multiple.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                   ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest           beefdbd8a1da       37.6MB         11.2MB
├─ linux/s390x          2b5b26e09ca2       11.9MB         3.46MB
├─ linux/arm64/v8       9cee2b382fe2       13.6MB         4.09MB
├─ linux/amd64          33735bd63cf8       12.1MB         3.63MB
├─ linux/arm/v6         50f635c8b04d           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v7         f2f82d424957           0B             0B
├─ linux/386            b3e87f642f5c           0B             0B
├─ linux/ppc64le        c7a6800e3dc5           0B             0B
└─ linux/riscv64        80cde017a105           0B             0B


build/docker image load -i image.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest        33735bd63cf8       12.1MB         3.63MB
└─ linux/amd64       33735bd63cf8       12.1MB         3.63MB
```

Loading produces a different kind of error in those cases;

```bash
docker image load -i image-multiple.tar --platform=linux/ppc64le
requested platform (linux/ppc64le) not found: NotFound: content digest sha256:c7a6800e3dc569a2d6e90627a2988f2a7339e6f111cdf6a0054ad1ff833e99b0: not found

docker image load -i image.tar --platform=linux/ppc64le
requested platform (linux/ppc64le) not found: image might be filtered out
```

review_comments:
This is to prevent unpacking to fail;

```
docker image load -i image-multiple.tar --platform=linux/s390x
Loaded image: alpine:latest
Error unpacking image alpine:latest: NotFound: content digest sha256:cf04c63912e16506c4413937c7f4579018e4bb25c272d989789cfba77b12f951: not found
```

For `platform == nil` this will always be true because matchRequestedOrDefault (that name could be better) will return a allPlatformsWithPreferenceMatcher which only *prefers* the default platform, but still matches any platform.

This is to handle gracefully a case where you only have a non-native platform available and you don' specify the `platform`.

So we should still have the special case for the `platform == nil` case.
